title: Per-core ringlet scheduler + page-coloring pinned buffers to reduce NUMA thrash
creator: Ava Chen
description: We observe intermittent latency spikes during prefill for long-context workloads caused by CPU-side scheduling jitter and NUMA memory placement thrash when staging buffers are allocated dynamically. This ticket implements a per-core "ringlet" scheduling layer that assigns small batches to core-local worker ringlets and couples it with page-coloring to allocate pinned stage buffers on the same NUMA node as the GPU DMA engines. The goal is to stabilize tail latency and reduce CPU-GPU handoff stalls without increasing average latency or peak memory usage.
acceptance_criteria: 95th and 99th token-level latency for synthetic long-context prefill workloads reduced by >= 30% compared to baseline across our standard host types
End-to-end prefill variance (stddev) reduced by >= 40% under mixed contention (background CPU load) on NUMA instances
No regression in throughput for short-context requests (< 64 tokens) within 5%
Automated regression tests and perf benchmarks added to CI; PR passes perf-sanity gating
design_decisions: Use per-core ringlet queues (lockless single-producer single-consumer) to avoid global threadpool contention; worker threads bind to a specific CPU core
Implement lightweight backpressure token per ringlet to cap in-flight microbatches and enable early fast-path fallback to a shared emergency queue
Page-coloring allocator: request hugetlb/pinned pages with explicit NUMA node hinting; fall back to normal pinned allocation if node unavailable
Keep DMA transfer logic unchanged; only change buffer placement and CPU-side scheduling to maintain hardware compatibility
Expose knobs (ringlet_count, ringlet_threshold, page_color_mode) behind runtime flags for gradual rollout and A/B testing
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Add core-local ringlet abstraction in host/prefill/scheduler module. Minimal API: enqueue(request), try_dequeue(), steal_from(neighbor_index)
Phase 1 tests: microbench SPSC enqueue/dequeue latency, synthetic steal behavior under overloaded ringlets
Phase 2: Integrate page-coloring allocator in host/arena with NUMA node discovery and fallback heuristics. Use libnuma on Linux and test on our staging GCP/EC2 images
Phase 3: Wire ringlet scheduling into prefill path: allocate pinned page-colored buffer from ringlet-local arena and schedule DMA; add metrics for ringlet queue depth and eviction rate
Phase 4: Add safe rollout: runtime flag defaults to off; expose metric-driven enablement in canary clusters; implement emergency drain to shared pool on OOM
Estimated risk: medium. Potential OOM on nodes with fragmented memory; mitigation: fall back to cross-node pinned allocation and emit warning metric
test_plan: Unit tests: ringlet enqueue/dequeue, steal invariants, allocator failure paths
Perf tests: long-context prefill (2048 tokens) p99/p95 measurements under no-load and with 60% background CPU load
Integration: run full e2e prefill+decode pipeline against model-catalog redwood/gpt-3-like on staging with pinned buffers; compare CPU utilization and DMA stall events
Chaos: simulate node memory fragmentation and force allocator fallback to ensure graceful degradation
CI: Add perf-sanity job that runs a 10-minute microbenchmark and checks p95 improvement trendline
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag. Deploy to canary cluster (10% of serving hosts) for 24h with detailed metrics (ringlet.latency.*, allocator.fallback.*)
If canary stable, expand to 50% for 48h and run customer-facing smoke tests (Chat and embeddings), monitor tail latency and OOM alerts
Full rollout to runtime-1.20 if no regressions and metrics meet acceptance criteria
If p99 worsens or OOMs observed, flip flag off and capture heap/profile for postmortem
